𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄

THE ANCIENT COVENANT RECORD

Volume One — Part One

The Torah — First Book

BERESHIT

In the Beginning

Chapters 1 through 11

Creation — Eden — The Fall — Qa'in and Hevel — Chanokh — The Flood — The Covenant of the Rainbow — The Tower of Bavel

PRIMARY MANUSCRIPT AUTHORITIES

Governed by the Bereshit Book-Level Critical Apparatus (v1.5, final frozen version) — full manuscript census, evidence hierarchy, and bibliography maintained there

1QGenesis (1Q1) — VERIFIED coverage of Gen 1:18–21; 3:11–14; 22:13–15; 23:17–19; 24:22–24

4QGend (4Q4), 4QGeng (4Q7), 4QGenh1 (4Q8/8a), 4QGenk (4Q10) — PROBABLE coverage of Genesis 1–3 generally

Samaritan Pentateuch — checked for ch.1, consistent with MT (no variant); major SP chronological variants flagged for chapters 5 and 11

Ethiopian Orit Ge'ez — Beta Israel Ancient Canon

COMPARATIVE NOTES AT END OF EVERY CHAPTER

DSS  ·  ORIT GE'EZ  ·  MASORETIC VARIANT  ·  CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitutions

All personal names in original Hebrew form throughout

BERESHIT — CREATION AND THE PRIMORDIAL HISTORY — CHAPTERS 1 THROUGH 11

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 1 The Six Days

1 In the beginning the Creator created the heavens and the earth.

2 Now the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of the Creator hovered over the face of the waters.

3 And the Creator said: Let there be light. And there was light.

4 And the Creator saw the light, that it was good; and the Creator divided the light from the darkness.

5 And the Creator called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.

6 And the Creator said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.

7 And the Creator made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament; and it was so.

8 And the Creator called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.

9 And the Creator said: Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear. And it was so.

10 And the Creator called the dry land Earth, and the gathering together of the waters he called Seas; and the Creator saw that it was good.

11 And the Creator said: Let the earth put forth grass, herb yielding seed, and fruit tree bearing fruit after its kind, in which is its seed, upon the earth. And it was so.

12 And the earth brought forth grass, herb yielding seed after its kind, and tree bearing fruit, in which is its seed, after its kind; and the Creator saw that it was good.

13 And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.

14 And the Creator said: Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years;

15 and let them be for lights in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth. And it was so.

16 And the Creator made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; and the stars.

17 And the Creator set them in the firmament of the heavens, to give light upon the earth,

18 and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness; and the Creator saw that it was good.

19 And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.

20 And the Creator said: Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let fowl fly above the earth in the open firmament of the heavens.

21 And the Creator created the great sea-monsters, and every living creature that creeps, with which the waters swarmed, after its kind, and every winged fowl after its kind; and the Creator saw that it was good.

22 And the Creator blessed them, saying: Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply on the earth.

23 And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.

24 And the Creator said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after its kind. And it was so.

25 And the Creator made the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and everything that creeps upon the ground after its kind; and the Creator saw that it was good.

26 And the Creator said: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.

27 And the Creator created man in his own image, in the image of the Creator created he him; male and female created he them.

28 And the Creator blessed them; and the Creator said to them: Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that creeps upon the earth.

29 And the Creator said: Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed — to you it shall be for food;

30 and to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to everything that creeps upon the earth, in which there is a living soul, every green herb for food. And it was so.

31 And the Creator saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 1QGenesis (1Q1): DJD I (Barthelemy), pp.49-50. This chapter's early verses (1-17) fall before 1Q1's earliest confirmed fragment (v.18); no direct citation for vv.1-17 this session. VERIFIED coverage begins at v.18 within this chapter. 4QGend (4Q4, single fragment, Gen 1), 4QGeng (4Q7, two fragments, Gen 1-2), 4QGenh1 (4Q8/8a, Gen 1:8-10 specifically), 4QGenk (4Q10, small fragments, Gen 1-3): PROBABLE general coverage per DJD XII (Davila) secondary citation; UNVERIFIED/OPEN at the level of a specific reading, since no direct transcription was obtained this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] Checked directly: secondary scholarship states the Genesis 1 creation account "remains consistent with the Masoretic tradition" -- a real, disclosed clean result. SP’s major, well-documented chronological variants are concentrated in the Genesis 5 and 11 genealogies, not this chapter -- flagged now for those future chapters rather than asserted here.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 2 -- רוח אלהים, "the spirit of the Creator" -- a genuine, disclosed ambiguity: רוח can denote spirit, wind, or breath, and the construction may function adjectivally ("a mighty wind") or as a direct actor. The majority reading is followed; the alternative is disclosed, not excluded. Verse 21 -- תנינם, "sea-monsters" -- the same term at the center of the Exodus 7:9 crux already documented in the frozen Shemot apparatus; its precise referent remains genuinely disputed. Verse 26 -- נעשה אדם, "let us make man" -- the cohortative plural is a well-known, genuine crux (royal/majestic plural; address to a divine council; or another explanation), disclosed as open, not resolved by translation.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 2 Eden — The Man and the Woman

1 And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.

2 And on the seventh day the Creator finished his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.

3 And the Creator blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it; because on it he rested from all his work which the Creator in creating had made.

4 These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that YHWH the Creator made earth and heavens.

5 No shrub of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for YHWH the Creator had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was no man to till the ground;

6 but a mist went up from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.

7 Then YHWH the Creator formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

8 And YHWH the Creator planted a garden eastward, in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

9 And out of the ground YHWH the Creator made to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

10 And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from there it was parted, and became four heads.

11 The name of the first is Pishon; that is it which encompasses the whole land of Chavilah, where there is gold;

12 and the gold of that land is good; there is bdellium and the onyx stone.

13 And the name of the second river is Gichon; the same is it that encompasses the whole land of Kush.

14 And the name of the third river is Chidekel; that is it which goes toward the east of Ashur. And the fourth river is the Perat.

15 And YHWH the Creator took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to work it and to keep it.

16 And YHWH the Creator commanded the man, saying: Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat;

17 but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat of it; for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.

18 And YHWH the Creator said: It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper corresponding to him.

19 And out of the ground YHWH the Creator formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them; and whatever the man called every living creature, that was its name.

20 And the man gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found a helper corresponding to him.

21 And YHWH the Creator caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept; and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.

22 And YHWH the Creator built the rib which he had taken from the man into a woman, and brought her to the man.

23 And the man said: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

24 Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

25 And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4QGeng (4Q7, two fragments, Gen 1-2) falls within this chapter per the book census -- PROBABLE general coverage, UNVERIFIED/OPEN at verse level. A real, specific claim requiring disclosure: secondary scholarship states that "several Qumran manuscripts" share the SP reading at v.2 (see Masoretic note) against MT. No specific manuscript designation was given by the source consulted -- recorded as a reported claim, not attributed to a named witness, and not elevated beyond PROBABLE.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] A real, substantive variant at v.2, with genuine chronological/theological stakes. MT reads that the Creator finished his work "on the seventh day." SP is reported to read "the sixth day" instead -- resolving the apparent tension of MT's phrasing (work "finished" on the very day set aside for rest). Secondary scholarship states this SP reading is independently supported by unspecified Qumran manuscripts. PROBABLE, not checked against a primary SP edition this session. Not adopted; MT's "seventh day" retained as base.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 1-3 continue chapter 1's exclusive use of אלהים alone. Verse 4 onward (11 occurrences) introduce the compound יהוה אלהים -- both divine designations in construct/apposition. Rendered "YHWH the Creator" at every occurrence, preserving both elements, consistent with the precedent established at Shemot 23:17 ("the Sovereign YHWH"). This is a real, well-documented textual seam noted in historical-critical source scholarship as a transition point; recorded as a textual observation, not asserted as settled fact.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 3 The Serpent and the Fall

1 Now the serpent was more subtle than any beast of the field which YHWH the Creator had made. And he said to the woman: Indeed, has the Creator said, You shall not eat of any tree of the garden?

2 And the woman said to the serpent: Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat;

3 but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, the Creator has said, You shall not eat of it, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.

4 And the serpent said to the woman: You shall not surely die;

5 for the Creator knows that in the day you eat of it, then your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be like the Creator, knowing good and evil.

6 And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to make one wise, she took of its fruit, and ate; and she gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

7 And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves loincloths.

8 And they heard the voice of YHWH the Creator walking in the garden in the cool of the day; and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of YHWH the Creator among the trees of the garden.

9 And YHWH the Creator called to the man, and said to him: Where are you?

10 And he said: I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

11 And he said: Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten of the tree of which I commanded you that you should not eat?

12 And the man said: The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.

13 And YHWH the Creator said to the woman: What is this you have done? And the woman said: The serpent deceived me, and I ate.

14 And YHWH the Creator said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle, and above all beasts of the field; on your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.

15 And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; they shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise their heel.

16 To the woman he said: I will greatly multiply your pain and your travail; in pain you shall bring forth children; and your desire shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you.

17 And to Adam he said: Because you have listened to the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree of which I commanded you, saying, You shall not eat of it — cursed is the ground for your sake; in toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life.

18 Thorns also and thistles it shall bring forth to you; and you shall eat the herb of the field.

19 In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the ground; for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return.

20 And the man called his wife's name Chavah, because she was the mother of all living.

21 And YHWH the Creator made for Adam and for his wife garments of skins, and clothed them.

22 And YHWH the Creator said: Behold, the man has become as one of us, to know good and evil; and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever —

23 therefore YHWH the Creator sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.

24 So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubim, and the flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter beyond the general Gen 1-3 coverage already logged for 4Q10 at chapter 1. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] A reported, single-source SP variant at v.1: one older cross-reference source (Treasury of Scripture Knowledge) states SP reads a form meaning "liar/deceiver" in place of "serpent." PROBABLE at best -- single lower-tier source, not corroborated by a second citation or a primary edition this session, and flagged with appropriate caution given the source’s age and general reliability relative to modern critical editions. Not adopted.

[CRITICAL NOTE] A real, disclosed pattern: vv.1(part)-5, within the serpent's and the woman's own reported speech, use אלהים alone; the narrative frame and YHWH's own direct speech (v.8 onward) resume the compound יהוה אלהים. Noted as a textual observation about this chapter's internal distribution, not asserted as evidence of separate authorship. Verse 5's כאלהים ("like the Creator" or "like the gods") and verse 22's כאחד ממנו ("as one of us") both involve the same genuine, disclosed plural-of-majesty/divine-council ambiguity already flagged at 1:26 -- not resolved here either.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 4 Kayin and Hevel

1 And the man knew Chavah his wife; and she conceived and bore Kayin, and said: I have gotten a man with YHWH.

2 And again she bore his brother Hevel. And Hevel was a keeper of sheep, but Kayin was a tiller of the ground.

3 And in the course of time it came to pass that Kayin brought of the fruit of the ground an offering to YHWH.

4 And Hevel, he also brought of the firstborn of his flock and of their fat. And YHWH had regard for Hevel and for his offering;

5 but for Kayin and for his offering he had no regard. And Kayin was very angry, and his face fell.

6 And YHWH said to Kayin: Why are you angry? And why has your face fallen?

7 If you do well, shall it not be lifted up? And if you do not do well, sin crouches at the door; and its desire is for you, but you may rule over it.

8 And Kayin spoke to Hevel his brother. And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Kayin rose up against Hevel his brother, and killed him.

9 And YHWH said to Kayin: Where is Hevel your brother? And he said: I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?

10 And he said: What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries to me from the ground.

11 And now cursed are you from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.

12 When you till the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength to you; a fugitive and a wanderer you shall be on the earth.

13 And Kayin said to YHWH: My punishment is greater than I can bear.

14 Behold, you have driven me out this day from the face of the land; and from your face I shall be hidden; and I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth; and it will come to pass, that whoever finds me will kill me.

15 And YHWH said to him: Therefore, whoever kills Kayin, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And YHWH set a sign for Kayin, lest anyone finding him should strike him.

16 And Kayin went out from the presence of YHWH, and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

17 And Kayin knew his wife; and she conceived, and bore Chanokh; and he built a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son Chanokh.

18 And to Chanokh was born Irad; and Irad begot Mechuya'el; and Mechuya'el begot Metusha'el; and Metusha'el begot Lemekh.

19 And Lemekh took for himself two wives; the name of one was Adah, and the name of the other Tzilah.

20 And Adah bore Yaval; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.

21 And his brother's name was Yuval; he was the father of all who play the harp and pipe.

22 And Tzilah, she also bore Tuval-Kayin, the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron; and the sister of Tuval-Kayin was Na'amah.

23 And Lemekh said to his wives: Adah and Tzilah, hear my voice; wives of Lemekh, listen to my speech; for I have slain a man for wounding me, and a young man for bruising me.

24 If Kayin is avenged sevenfold, truly Lemekh seventy-sevenfold.

25 And Adam knew his wife again; and she bore a son, and called his name Shet, for she said: the Creator has appointed for me another seed instead of Hevel, for Kayin killed him.

26 And to Shet, to him also a son was born, and he called his name Enosh; then men began to call upon the name of YHWH.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. 4Q252 (Commentary on Genesis A) is documented as touching material from this general narrative region in some catalogs, but as a pesher/commentary genre, not a running-text witness -- not treated as manuscript evidence per the standing genre-disclosure rule. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] A real, well-documented "missing speech" pattern, directly comparable to the one already catalogued in the frozen Shemot apparatus (10:2, 11:3). At v.8, MT states "Kayin spoke to Hevel his brother" but supplies no content for what was said, before immediately narrating the murder. Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint both independently supply the missing words, reported as "Let us go out to the field." PROBABLE, corroborated by two independent witness traditions per secondary citation -- not checked against primary editions of either this session. Not adopted; MT’s gap is preserved faithfully rather than filled.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 1’s קניתי איש את יהוה ("I have gotten a man with YHWH") contains a genuine minor interpretive crux in the preposition את, which can carry a sense of instrumentality ("with the help of") or accompaniment ("together with") -- the majority reading is followed, the alternative disclosed. Verse 25 uses אלהים alone in Chavah’s naming statement for Shet, while verse 26 explicitly marks the invocation of the name YHWH by name as beginning only with Enosh’s generation -- a self-aware internal marker about the divine name’s usage history, noted as the text’s own claim, not independently adjudicated.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 5 The Generations of Adam

1 This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that the Creator created man, in the likeness of the Creator he made him;

2 male and female he created them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.

3 And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Shet.

4 And the days of Adam after he begot Shet were eight hundred years; and he begot sons and daughters.

5 And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years; and he died.

6 And Shet lived a hundred and five years, and begot Enosh.

7 And Shet lived after he begot Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.

8 And all the days of Shet were nine hundred and twelve years; and he died.

9 And Enosh lived ninety years, and begot Keinan.

10 And Enosh lived after he begot Keinan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.

11 And all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years; and he died.

12 And Keinan lived seventy years, and begot Mahalal'el.

13 And Keinan lived after he begot Mahalal'el eight hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters.

14 And all the days of Keinan were nine hundred and ten years; and he died.

15 And Mahalal'el lived sixty-five years, and begot Yered.

16 And Mahalal'el lived after he begot Yered eight hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters.

17 And all the days of Mahalal'el were eight hundred ninety-five years; and he died.

18 And Yered lived a hundred sixty-two years, and begot Chanokh.

19 And Yered lived after he begot Chanokh eight hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.

20 And all the days of Yered were nine hundred sixty-two years; and he died.

21 And Chanokh lived sixty-five years, and begot Metushelach.

22 And Chanokh walked with the Creator after he begot Metushelach three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.

23 And all the days of Chanokh were three hundred sixty-five years.

24 And Chanokh walked with the Creator, and he was not, for the Creator took him.

25 And Metushelach lived a hundred eighty-seven years, and begot Lemekh.

26 And Metushelach lived after he begot Lemekh seven hundred eighty-two years, and begot sons and daughters.

27 And all the days of Metushelach were nine hundred sixty-nine years; and he died.

28 And Lemekh lived a hundred eighty-two years, and begot a son.

29 And he called his name Noach, saying: This one shall comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, from the ground which YHWH has cursed.

30 And Lemekh lived after he begot Noach five hundred ninety-five years, and begot sons and daughters.

31 And all the days of Lemekh were seven hundred seventy-seven years; and he died.

32 And Noach was five hundred years old; and Noach begot Shem, Cham, and Yefet.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The major, book-level-flagged chronological variant, now fully documented. MT, SP, and LXX diverge substantially in this chapter's patriarchal ages. LXX systematically adds 100 years to each patriarch's age at his son's birth (compensating by subtracting the same 100 from the remainder, preserving each total lifespan) for the first five patriarchs; SP matches MT for those same five. The real divergence begins at Yered: MT/SP both read 162 at Chanokh's birth, while proto-LXX implies 62. From that point, Metushelach and Lemekh diverge substantially across all three traditions (MT: 187/782/969 and 182/595/777; SP: 67/653/720 and 53/600/653; LXX: 167/802/969 and 188/565/753) -- SP's changes appear to shorten these three patriarchs' lives so none survive past the Flood, while LXX's inflation leaves only Metushelach surviving 14 years past it in early copies. PROBABLE -- this comparison is drawn from a secondary synthesis (Journal of Creation 29.2, 2015, Cosner & Carter) that itself cites primary text-critical scholarship (Klein 1974, Hendel 1998, Wenham 1987); the specific SP and LXX figures have not been independently checked against a primary SP or LXX critical edition this session. Disclosed explicitly: that synthesizing source argues for MT's chronological superiority on text-critical and doctrinal grounds -- only the underlying textual-variant data is used here; the source's own argumentative conclusions are not adopted, consistent with the project's historical-boundary scope and its exclusion of theological harmonization. MT's numbers are retained as base throughout this reconstruction.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 22 and 24's אלהים ("Chanokh walked with the Creator") are the sole divine-name occurrences in an otherwise name-free genealogical chapter (v.29's יהוה is the only other exception, in Lemekh's naming-speech for Noach) -- both rendered per standing policy. Numerical/genealogical terminology rendered with all figures literal throughout, consistent with standing translation philosophy; no number rounded or adjusted.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 6 The Nefilim — Noach and the Ark

1 And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,

2 that the sons of the Creator saw the daughters of men, that they were fair; and they took wives for themselves of all whom they chose.

3 And YHWH said: My spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he also is flesh; therefore his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.

4 The Nefilim were on the earth in those days, and also after that, when the sons of the Creator came in to the daughters of men, and they bore children to them; the same were the mighty men who were of old, the men of renown.

5 And YHWH saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.

6 And YHWH regretted that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.

7 And YHWH said: I will blot out man whom I have created from the face of the earth — man, and beast, and creeping thing, and fowl of the air — for I regret that I have made them.

8 But Noach found favor in the eyes of YHWH.

9 These are the generations of Noach. Noach was in his generations a righteous man, blameless; Noach walked with the Creator.

10 And Noach begot three sons: Shem, Cham, and Yefet.

11 And the earth was corrupt before the Creator, and the earth was filled with violence.

12 And the Creator saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.

13 And the Creator said to Noach: The end of all flesh has come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

14 Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; you shall make rooms in the ark, and shall cover it inside and out with pitch.

15 And this is how you shall make it: the length of the ark three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.

16 You shall make a light for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from above; and set the door of the ark in its side; you shall make it with lower, second, and third decks.

17 And I, behold, I bring the flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens; everything that is on the earth shall perish.

18 But I will establish my covenant with you; and you shall come into the ark, you, and your sons, and your wife, and your sons' wives with you.

19 And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every kind you shall bring into the ark, to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.

20 Of the fowl after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind — two of every kind shall come to you, to keep them alive.

21 And you, take for yourself of all food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; and it shall be for food for you, and for them.

22 Thus Noach did; according to all that the Creator commanded him, so he did.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. Extra-biblical Enoch and Book of Giants material (e.g., 1QapGen ar, 4Q203, 4Q530-533) engages this chapter's Nefilim narrative thematically, but per the standing genre-disclosure rule these are not running-text witnesses to Bereshit and are excluded from the manuscript census -- noted here only to disclose the connection, not to claim it as textual evidence. 7 And Noach went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 11 Bavel — The Generations of Shem — Terach

1 And the whole earth was of one language and of one speech.

2 And it came to pass, as they journeyed east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.

3 And they said to one another: Come, let us make bricks, and burn them thoroughly. And they had brick for stone, and tar for mortar.

4 And they said: Come, let us build ourselves a city, and a tower, with its top in the heavens, and let us make ourselves a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.

6 And YHWH said: Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language; and this is what they begin to do; and now nothing will be withheld from them, which they purpose to do.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The second major, book-level-flagged chronological variant (see 5:maso and OQ-4), now fully documented. Compared to MT, both SP and LXX inflate the Genesis 11 chronology, but SP uniquely adds a total-lifespan checksum to each patriarch's entry (a feature not in MT), retaining the same total lifespan as MT for all nine patriarchs -- best explained as an intentional harmonization duplicating the Genesis 5 formula, itself a documented SP tendency (harmonizing parallel passages, e.g. the Decalogue material already noted in the frozen Shemot apparatus). The LXX inflation has no such checksum and is described in the secondary literature as 'uncontrolled' by comparison. One further reported divergence: at Ever's entry (v.17), the source states LXX (370) and SP (270, following the same -100 pattern) both differ from MT's 430, with the secondary literature proposing MT's figure resulted from a scribal metathesis of two similar Hebrew phrases -- disclosed as a reported textual-critical argument, not independently verified against a primary edition this session. PROBABLE throughout; same sourcing and same explicit non-adoption of that source's own doctrinal argumentation as documented at 5:maso. MT's figures are retained as base.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 1-9 (the Bavel narrative) use יהוה exclusively, continuing the established alternation pattern. Verse 26's report that Terach was seventy when he begot 'Avram, Nachor, and Haran' (in that textual order) does not by itself establish Avram's birth order or Terach's exact age at Avram's specific birth -- a genuine, long-noted ambiguity (bridging into ch.12's departure account) that this reconstruction does not resolve by assumption.
